Subject: RFI: Dedicated capacity sizing for inference fleet (initial data)

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for taking our RFI. We're trying to lock down committed capacity for a private deployment (VPC) that will host several clinical-NLP models. To help our procurement committee, can you confirm the following baseline items and tell us what data you need to size the dedicated pool and compute a month-1 commit?

Key asks:
- Expected per-model throughput (QPS) at p50/p95 given sequence lengths 128/512 tokens
- Best-fit GPU family recommendations for quantized 4-bit weights (cost vs tail-latency tradeoffs)
- Burst sizing: how much headroom (as % of committed pool) we should allocate for unpredictable spikes
- Fallback policy options if committed capacity is temporarily saturated (eg. lower-cost model variants, regional failover)

We can share anonymized sample traffic and a short evaluation prompt set if that will speed things up. Our target SLO is 200 ms p95 for interactive workflows (seq=128) and 500 ms p95 for batch inference (seq=512).

Please respond with the info you can provide this week. Procurement needs the initial sizing worksheet by Friday.

Best,
Sofia
Sofia Marquez
Senior Procurement Manager
Nimbus Health

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear asks. Quick summary below and a short list of data we'll need to produce a draft committed-capacity workbook. I'm looping in Kar tik and Laura for GPU-fit and pricing inputs.

Short answers (high level):
- p50/p95 guidance depends strongly on model family and quantization; for many Llama-style models quantized to 4-bit we typically see ~20-30% faster per-token throughput vs fp16 on A10/A6000-class (price-sensitive) and ~2-3x throughput improvement on H100-family with tensor-core kernels for longer sequences.
- For your p95 targets: if you require 200 ms p95 at seq=128 for interactive, recommended commit is: enough slots to sustain peak steady QPS of ~120 concurrent interactive requests (we'll refine when we see sample QPS).
- Burst sizing: we recommend a 25-40% burst lane depending on tolerance for preemption and cost sensitivity.
- Fallbacks: model-variant degrade + regional fallback is typical; can automate routing so that non-critical requests fall back to lower-cost quantized variants.

Data we need to size accurately:
1) Representative QPS profile (minute-resolution for a week or hourly for a month)
2) Percent of requests that are interactive vs batch, and target percentiles for each
3) Typical input token distribution (p10/p50/p90) for each workload
4) Examples of the two model families you expect to serve (or we can run perf on your artifacts)

Deliverables we'll produce this week after we get the sample: committed-capacity workbook (slotting + GPU family mix), a burst allocation proposal, and a short runbook for overflow/fallback.

I'll attach a draft workbook and a short quantization-fitment matrix in my next email once we have the sample traffic.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Markus — a couple of technical clarifications to include in the workbook so procurement has operational knobs: 

1) GPU families we should present (three-tier): cost-optimized (A10/A6000-class), balanced (A100-80GB equivalent), performance (H100-class). For quantized 4-bit workloads, the balanced tier often gives the best $/p95 for seq<=256.
2) Slotting approach: we propose two pooling strategies in the workbook — homogeneous pools (single GPU family) versus mixed-slot pools (autoscaler respects preferred GPUs). We should show cost vs failure-domain resilience for both.
3) Preemption/fair-share policy: show how autoscaler will reclaim burst lanes and the expected impact on p95.
4) Model-variant sizes: include token-per-request cost estimates for the full model and two quantized variants (4-bit and 8-bit).

I'll draft the GPU mix tab and run some synthetic perf numbers for seq=128 and 512 to seed the workbook.

Sofia — attaching the draft workbook (RI_Dedicated_Workbook_v2.xlsx) and a short matrix that summarizes the quantization impact per GPU family (quantization-fitment-matrix.pdf). Highlights below so procurement can read quickly: 

Executive summary:
- Suggested month-1 commitment: 48 balanced slots (A100-equivalent) with a 35% burst lane (equivalent of ~17 additional slots) to cover morning spikes and short-lived surges while preserving p95 SLOs.
- Rationale: Based on your daytime steady-state of ~40 interactive QPS and observed spikes to 180 QPS, 48 slots sustain the interactive load with headroom for batch-to-interactive interference when autoscaler is reclaiming resources.
- Quantization impact: 4-bit model variants deliver ~1.6x token throughput vs fp16 on balanced GPUs at similar tail-latency for seq<=256; for seq=512 we recommend H100-class if batch job latency matters.
- Fallback strategy: primary — model-variant degrade (auto-route non-critical calls to 4-bit); secondary — regional failover to another dedicated pool with async buffering for non-interactive jobs.

Operational notes (tabs inside workbook):
- Slotting tab: shows three SKU examples (homogeneous A100 pool, mixed pool with A10 burst lane, H100 for heavy batch).
- Cost sensitivity tab: delta of monthly commit cost vs burst percent and vs using mixed pools.
- Runbook tab: step-by-step for reclaiming burst lanes, toggling quantized variant rollout, and issuing SLA credits in case of extended overflow.

Next steps: we can run perf on your provided artifacts later this week; if results show higher per-request token counts we'll iterate the workbook. Please confirm if procurement wants the workbook updated with your actual container perf numbers — we can prioritize that for tomorrow.

Regards,
Markus Klein
